'''''John Proctor Is the Villain''''' is a [[Play (theatre)|stage play]] written by American playwright [[Kimberly Belflower]]. It is a revisionist take on the classic American play ''[[The Crucible]]'' by [[Arthur Miller]], centering on a group of modern-day high school students and their interpretation of the historical events the play is based on.<ref>{{Cite web |last=SpotCo |title=Cast |url=https://johnproctoristhevillain.com/cast |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=JOHN PROCTOR IS THE VILLAIN {{!}} Official Broadway Website |language=en}}</ref>

== Summary ==
''John Proctor Is the Villain'' is set in a high-school classroom in a small, rural Georgia town in 2018.<ref name="Gyarkye j667">{{cite web |last=Gyarkye |first=Lovia |date=April 15, 2025 |title='John Proctor Is the Villain' Review: Sadie Sink Makes an Exciting Broadway Return in a Sharp and Funny Re-Interpretation of 'The Crucible' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/arts/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-sadie-sink-broadway-1236190543/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> Carter Smith is the English teacher for several 11th-graders—the straight-A student Beth, the new transfer student Nell, the wealthy girl Ivy, the pastor's daughter Raelynn, the slightly awkward Mason, and Raelynn's boyfriend Lee.<ref name="Holdren e472">{{cite web |last=Holdren |first=Sara |date=April 15, 2025 |title=A Crucible of Teen Drama: John Proctor Is the Villain |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/theater-review-john-proctor-villain-belflower.html |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[Vulture.com|Vulture]]}}</ref><ref name="nyt-2025-04-15">{{Cite news |last=Green |first=Jesse |date=April 15, 2025 |title=Review: In 'John Proctor Is the Villain,' It's the Girls vs. the Men |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/14/theater/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-sink.html |access-date=June 21, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name="Lewis u120">{{cite web |last=Lewis |first=Christian |date=April 15, 2025 |title='John Proctor Is the Villain' Review: Broadway Play Is a Powerful, Pop-Inflected Retort to 'The Crucible' |url=https://variety.com/2025/legit/reviews/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-broadway-sadie-sink-1236368941/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> Mr. Smith assigns the students the play ''[[The Crucible]]'', the protagonist of which is [[John Proctor (Salem witch trials)|John Proctor]], who was convicted of witchcraft during the [[Salem witch trials]].<ref name="Holdren e472" /><ref name="Lewis u120" /> Beth forms the school's feminist club, with Mr. Smith as its sponsor.<ref name="Lewis u120" /> Tensions rise when Raelynn's estranged friend Shelby returns to school after a prolonged absence.<ref name="nyt-2025-04-15" /><ref name="Gyarkye j667" /> During the semester, Ivy's father is accused of [[sexual harassment]] during the [[MeToo movement|#MeToo movement]],<ref name="Lewis u120" /> a source of controversy in the small town,<ref name="Gyarkye j667" /> causing her to withdraw from the club. Lee tries to repair his relationship with Raelynn (having cheated on her with Shelby).<ref name="Holdren e472" /> Miss Gallagher, the school's guidance counselor, mediates various issues between Mr. Smith and the students.<ref name="Lewis u120" /> Over the course of the year, the class discusses ''The Crucible'''s themes of power, gender inequality, and female sexuality. In a tense class period, Shelby loudly disagrees with Mr. Smith's insistence that John Proctor is a good man, and announces that Mr. Smith had been sexually abusing her over the last year.

The accusation causes waves throughout the town. Despite her feminist ideals, Beth deeply admires Mr. Smith and is reluctant to believe Shelby, further straining relations among the girls. Nell and Mason grow closer, but Mason insults Shelby's perceived promiscuity, causing her to take off. Raelynn, her reluctant assigned partner for an interpretative project based on the play, follows her and the two reconcile.<ref name="Lewis u120" /> Shelby admits that Mr. Smith's abuse of power had left her feeling vulnerable, which is why she slept with Lee. Mr. Smith is allowed to continue teaching and turns his attentions to Beth. On the day of the project presentation, Ms. Gallagher, who has been assigned by the school board to supervise Mr. Smith's class, reveals to him she has been aware of rumors of his predatory behavior since college. Raelynn and Shelby, acting as [[Elizabeth Proctor]] and [[Abigail Williams]] from the play, imagine a world where their actions are not defined by the men in their lives. They begin dancing, echoing Abigail's dance in the woods. Mr. Smith angrily attempts to stop the performance, but the girls' cathartic dance is supported by Nell, Mason, and Ms. Gallagher. In the final moments of the dance, Beth stands from her desk and takes a step towards the girls; the lights go out, leaving the audience to wonder if Beth joins them.<ref>{{cite web |title=JOHN PROCTOR IS THE VILLAIN final |url=https://www.cliffsnotes.com/study-notes/24356801 |access-date=September 5, 2025 |website=sparknotes.com}}</ref>

''John Proctor Is the Villain'' includes several songs by pop artists such as [[Lorde]] and [[Taylor Swift]].<ref name="Lewis u120" /> In some productions, these songs are performed in between scenes, as well as before the first scene and during the last scene.<ref name="Milzoff j108">{{cite web |last=Milzoff |first=Rebecca |date=June 5, 2025 |title=In Broadway's 'John Proctor Is the Villain,' Lorde, Taylor Swift & Pop Music Have Starring Roles |url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/john-proctor-is-the-villain-broadway-lorde-taylor-swift-pop/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Billboard}}</ref> The Broadway production used ominous sounds and flickering lights to denote the transitions between each scene.<ref name="Travis n089">{{cite web |last=Travis |first=Emlyn |date=April 14, 2025 |title=Sadie Sink and 'John Proctor Is the Villain' cast shine in 'Crucible'-inspired play |url=https://ew.com/john-proctor-is-the-villain-sadie-sink-broadway-play-review-11714446 |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=EW.com}}</ref><ref name="Hofler r071">{{cite web |last=Hofler |first=Robert |date=April 15, 2025 |title='John Proctor Is the Villain' Broadway Review: Sadie Sink Deconstructs 'The Crucible' |url=https://www.thewrap.com/john-proctor-is-the-villain-broadway-review-sadie-sink/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=TheWrap}}</ref> Belflower received permission to use excerpts from ''The Crucible'' from Arthur Miller's estate.<ref name="nyt-2025-04-15" /><ref>[https://www.dramatists.com/cgi-bin/db/single.asp?index=0&key=6421 ''Dramatists.com John Proctor is the Villain licensing''] accessed 10/20/2024</ref>

==Production history==
[[File:John Proctor is the Villain Booth Theatre exterior.jpg|thumb|right|180px|''John Proctor Is the Villain'' signage at the Booth Theater on Broadway]]

===Developmental workshops and productions (2018-2019)===
The play was originally commissioned by [http://www.thefarmtheater.org The Farm Theater] for their College Collaboration Project and first workshopped in 2018 and 2019 in three colleges theatre departments: [[Centre College]] in [[Danville, Kentucky]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goff |first=Jennifer |title=John Proctor is the Villain |url=http://www.jennifergoff.com/john-proctor-is-the-villain.html |access-date=2024-10-10 |place=Centre College}}</ref>, [[Furman University]] in [[Greenville, South Carolina]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Underwood |first=Tina |date=2024-10-18 |title=Furman Theatre collaboration with Belflower to hit Broadway |url=https://www.furman.edu/news/furman-theatre-collaboration-with-belflower-to-hit-broadway/ |access-date=2023-10-21 |website=Furman News |publisher=[[Furman University]] |language=en-US}}</ref>, and [[Rollins College]] in [[Winter Park, Florida]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Murray-Campbell |first1=Anna |title=Review: Students shine in ‘John Proctor is the Villain’ debut |url=https://www.thesandspur.org/review-students-shine-in-john-proctor-is-the-villain-debut/ |access-date=18 June 2026 |publisher=The Sandspur |date=20 February 2019}}</ref>. The play was also workshopped as part of the [[Ojai Playwrights Conference]]'s New Works Festival in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Past Plays |url=https://www.ojaiplays.org/past-plays |website=Ojai Playwrights Conference |publisher=Ojai Playwrights Conference |access-date=18 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Washington, D.C. (2022) ===
The play was first professionally produced by [[Studio Theatre (Washington, D.C.)|Studio Theatre]] in Washington D.C in 2022, running from April 27 until June 5, directed by Marti Lyons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=John Proctor is the Villain |url=https://playbill.com/production/john-procter-is-the-villain-regional-studio-theatre-2022 |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=[[Playbill]]}}</ref> Since then, it has been performed by various small theaters and colleges in the DMV area, including [[Georgetown University]]'s Mask and Bauble Dramatic Society in 2023, until its Broadway premiere in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howes |first=Sophia |date=2023-10-27 |title=A glorious 'John Proctor Is the Villain' from Mask and Bauble at GU |url=https://dctheaterarts.org/2023/10/27/a-glorious-john-proctor-is-the-villain-from-mask-and-bauble-at-gu/ |access-date=2025-07-28 |website=DC Theater Arts |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Boston (2024) ===
In 2024, another production was staged at the [[Huntington Theatre Company]] in Boston, running from February 8 until March 10, directed by Margot Bordelon.<ref>[https://www.huntingtontheatre.org/whats-on/john-proctor-is-the-villain/''Huntington Theatre Company John Proctor''] accessed 10/20/2024</ref> The Boston production was nominated for six [[Elliot Norton Awards]], winning Outstanding Play, Large; and Outstanding Ensemble.

=== Broadway (2025) ===
The play premiered on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] in 2025, directed by [[Danya Taymor]] and starring [[Sadie Sink]]. Previews began on March 20, 2025, with an opening date of April 14, 2025 at the [[Booth Theatre]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Greg |date=2024-10-17 |title='Stranger Things' Actor Sadie Sink To Star In Broadway Comedy 'John Proctor Is The Villain' |url=https://deadline.com/2024/10/sadie-sink-broadway-1236118721/ |access-date=2024-10-10 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The show opened to positive reviews and received seven Tony Award nominations, including Best Play.<ref name=":0" /> Before the play officially opened, its run was extended by two weeks to July 6,<ref name="Hall">{{cite web |last=Hall |first=Margaret |date=May 27, 2025 |title=John Proctor is the Villain Extends Broadway Run |url=https://playbill.com/article/john-proctor-is-the-villain-extends-broadway-run |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Playbill}}</ref> then by another week to July 13.<ref name="Hall"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Chachowski |first=Richard |date=May 27, 2025 |title=Popular Tony-Nominated Broadway Play Receives Summer Extension |url=https://parade.com/news/john-proctor-broadway-extension |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Parade}}</ref> That June, the play's run was extended again to August 31,<ref>{{cite web |last=Hall |first=Margaret |date=June 5, 2025 |title=John Proctor is the Villain Extends Broadway Run Through Summer |url=https://playbill.com/article/john-proctor-is-the-villain-extends-broadway-run-through-summer |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Playbill}}</ref> with [[Chiara Aurelia]] replacing Sink in the role of Shelby Holcomb after July 13.<ref>{{cite web |last=Culwell-Block |first=Logan |last2=Hall |first2=Margaret |date=June 12, 2025 |title=Chiara Aurelia Will Join Broadway's John Proctor is the Villain |url=https://playbill.com/article/chiara-aurelia-will-join-broadways-john-proctor-is-the-villain |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Playbill}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Russo |first=Gillian |date=June 12, 2025 |title=Chiara Aurelia to join 'John Proctor Is the Villain' Broadway cast |url=https://www.newyorktheatreguide.com/theatre-news/news/chiara-aurelia-to-join-john-proctor-is-the-villain-cast |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=New York Theatre Guide}}</ref> The show ended its Broadway run on September 7, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=SpotCo |title=JOHN PROCTOR IS THE VILLAIN {{!}} Official Broadway Website |url=https://johnproctoristhevillain.com/ |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=JOHN PROCTOR IS THE VILLAIN {{!}} Official Broadway Website |language=en}}</ref>

=== London (2026) ===
The play made its European premiere at [[London|London's]] [[Royal Court Theatre]] from March 20, running for a limited engagement until April 25, 2026. The entire Broadway creative team reunited, while a whole new cast was formed for this production.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-28 |title=John Proctor is the Villain to have UK premiere |url=https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/john-proctor-is-the-villain-to-have-uk-premiere_1700100/ |access-date=2025-10-28 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Hall | first=Margaret | title=Kimberly Belflower's John Proctor Is the Villain To Play London in 2026 | website=Playbill | date=October 28, 2025 | url=https://playbill.com/article/kimberly-belflowers-john-proctor-is-the-villain-to-play-london-in-2026 | access-date=October 30, 2025}}</ref> It received critical acclaim and sold out its entire engagement.

The cast includes [[Holly Howden Gilchrist]], [[Lauryn Ajufo]], [[Donal Finn]] and [[Sadie Soverall]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.londontheatre.co.uk/theatre-news/news/full-cast-revealed-for-john-proctor-is-the-villain-at-the-royal-court|first=Olivia|last=Rook|date=2 February 2026|access-date=5 February 2026|title=Full cast revealed for 'John Proctor Is the Villain' at the Royal Court|website=London Theatre}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=John Proctor is the Villain cast has been announced |url=https://royalcourttheatre.com/stories/john-proctor-is-the-villain-cast-has-been-announced/ |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=Royal Court Theatre |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/stage/2026/mar/27/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-royal-court-theatre|date=27 March 2026|access-date=29 March 2026|website=The Guardian|first=Arifa|last=Akbar|author-link=Arifa Akbar|title=John Proctor Is the Villain review – Arthur Miller’s classic sparks a #MeToo moment}}</ref>

=== West End (2027) ===
The play is set to transfer to the [[Wyndham's Theatre|Wyndham’s Theatre]] in the [[West End theatre|West End]] for a limited 12-week engagement from February 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-20 |title=John Proctor is the Villain to transfer to the West End next year |url=https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/john-proctor-is-the-villain-to-transfer-to-the-west-end-next-year_1718783/ |access-date=2026-04-21 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Broadway ===
[[Jesse Green (theatre critic)|Jesse Green]] of the ''[[New York Times]]'' wrote that Belflower "smartly keeps the play from becoming a polemic by moving on several tracks at once" by combining such elements as "pure high school comedy", pop music, and feminist interpretations of classic works.<ref name="nyt-2025-04-15" /> Reviewers for ''[[AmNewYork]]'' and ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'' wrote that ''John Proctor Is the Villain'' was particularly relevant during the [[second presidency of Donald Trump]], during which references to [[diversity, equity, and inclusion]] initiatives were being discouraged by the U.S. government.<ref name="Holdren e472" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Windman |first=Matt |date=April 14, 2025 |title=John Proctor is the Villain: Salem's hero gets #MeToo'd |url=https://www.amny.com/entertainment/theater/review-john-proctor-is-the-villain/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=amNewYork}}</ref> A reviewer for ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote that ''John Proctor Is the Villain'' interpreted ''The Crucible'' through a feminist lens, "demonstrating the power of feminine solidarity and rage",<ref name="Lewis u120" /> a sentiment shared by an ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' critic.<ref name="Travis n089" /> Another reviewer for ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' called the storyline "a poignant story of girlhood and empowering friendships".<ref name="Gyarkye j667" /> Conversely, a writer for ''[[TheWrap]]'' described the short scenes as characteristic of novice playwrights,<ref name="Hofler r071" /> and a ''[[New York Daily News]]'' writer said: "I wish "John Proctor" made its very fair point about girls forging their own narratives with more ambivalence and less certitude."<ref>{{cite web |last=Jones |first=Chris |date=April 15, 2025 |title=BROADWAY REVIEW: 'John Proctor is the Villain' with Sadie Sink is lively if predictable drama |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/04/14/broadway-review-john-proctor-is-the-villain-with-sadie-sink-is-lively-if-predictable-drama/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[New York Daily News]]}}</ref>

=== London ===
Sarah Hemming of the ''[[Financial Times]]'' described the play as "a joyous, blazingly intelligent play...at once a restless interrogation of the role of art in defining and expressing who we are; a compassionate, funny portrayal of what it means to be a teenage girl; and a furious appraisal of the way power games repeat across generations."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hemming |first=Sarah |date=31 March 2026 |title=John Proctor is the Villain review — The Crucible seen through the eyes of #MeToo-era schoolgirls |url=https://www.ft.com/content/84f9336f-39c7-433b-b095-355eae869216?syn-25a6b1a6=1 |website=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref> Sarah Crompton from [[WhatsOnStage.com|''WhatsOnStage'']] wrote that the play is "a witty and convincing picture of teenage girlhood, its brightness, hopes and fears."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-27 |title=John Proctor is the Villain review – The Crucible on trial at the Royal Court |url=https://www.whatsonstage.com/news/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-the-crucible-on-trial-at-the-royal-court_1716579/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |language=en-US}}</ref> Alice Saville of ''[[The Independent]]'' wrote that Belflower's play "like The Crucible...shows how quickly new ideas can contaminate a small, contained environment, spreading like penicillin spores on white bread. And this town doesn’t want to take its medicine."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-27 |title=John Proctor is the Villain is a brilliantly cathartic riff on The Crucible – review |url=https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/theatre-dance/reviews/john-proctor-is-the-villain-review-royal-court-b2946888.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>j

== Film adaptation ==
On July 18, 2025, it was announced that [[Universal Pictures]] successfully outbid other studios for the rights to the play, which will be adapted by Belflower into a feature film. [[Tina Fey]], [[Eric Gurian]], [[Marc Platt (producer)|Marc Platt]], Adam Siegel and Jared LeBoff are producing, and actress [[Sadie Sink]] is an executive producer.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Galuppo|first=Mia|title=Tina Fey, Marc Platt Team for 'John Proctor Is the Villain' Movie at Universal (Exclusive)|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/tina-fey-marc-platt-john-proctor-villain-movie-1236318909/|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=July 18, 2025|access-date=July 18, 2025}}</ref> Taymor, who directed the original play, signed on as director.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://deadline.com/2026/01/john-proctor-is-the-villain-movie-universal-danya-taymor-1236702547/|title= ‘John Proctor Is The Villain’ Movie At Universal Taps Danya Taymor To Direct|date= January 29, 2026|access-date= January 30, 2026|first= Justin|last= Kroll|work= Deadline Hollywood}}</ref>

extract: John Proctor Is the Villain is a stage play written by American playwright Kimberly Belflower. It is a revisionist take on the classic American play The Crucible by Arthur Miller, centering on a group of modern-day high school students and their interpretation of the historical events the play is based on.
